result.summary: Introduces a minimal `linux-base-gcc` toolchain variant in Guix for static non-GUI Linux builds, configuring `libstdc++` with `--disable-wchar_t`, `--enable-clocale=generic`, and `--with-libstdcxx-zoneinfo=no`. It also disables the experimental `libstdc++fs` library across Linux GCC builds and adds a patch in `depends` so Boost Test compiles without `std::wcrtomb`.
result.problem: Static non-GUI Linux release binaries link unused `libstdc++` components—such as wide-character handling, chrono timezone information, and experimental filesystem TS routines—unnecessarily inflating binary sizes.
evidence: PR description benchmarks show non-GUI binary sizes decrease by roughly 0.48 MB across all tools (bitcoind shrinks from 17.75 MB to 17.27 MB, bitcoin-cli from 8.20 MB to 7.72 MB).
result.scope_notes: Touches Guix build toolchain definitions and adds a patch to depends Boost Test.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased with no substantive changes to the approach or scope.
result.card: Introduces a minimal linux-base-gcc toolchain variant in Guix for non-GUI Linux release builds, disabling unused libstdc++ features including wide-character support, zoneinfo tables, and the experimental filesystem TS library. Boost Test in depends is patched to use unqualified wcrtomb to retain compatibility without libstdc++ wchar_t support. This reduces release binary sizes for non-GUI tools like bitcoind and bitcoin-cli by approximately 0.5 MB.

risk.why: Alters GCC configuration for release binaries, which could introduce runtime failures in locale or date-time handling if any non-GUI component inadvertently relies on disabled libstdc++ features.
